title: Length of the Longest Valid Substring
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_set<string> ban: up to 10^5 entries, total chars ≤ 10^6 → O(F·L)
- temporary substr strings: ≤ 10 chars each, not persistent → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input word, forbidden vector
approach: Use a sliding window [left, right] over `word`. Since every forbidden string has length ≤ 10, for each new `right` we only need to inspect the ≤ 10 substrings ending at `right`. If `word[right-L+1 .. right]` is forbidden, the window cannot contain it, so we push `left` to `right-L+2` (taking the max over all such constraints, since the tightest one wins). The answer is the maximum window size seen. Correctness: any forbidden substring ending at some index `j` was detected when `right == j` and forced `left` past its start, so the window never contains a forbidden substring.
hints: Each forbidden string is at most 10 characters long. For a fixed right end of a candidate substring, how many distinct ending positions of forbidden patterns could possibly overlap that right end?

Use a sliding window with a hash set of forbidden strings. At `right = 7` in "cbaaaabc", check substrings "c", "bc", "abc", "aabc", ... ending at index 7; none are in {"aaa","cb"}, so the window [4,7] of length 4 is valid.

**Single character forbidden** - the forbidden list contains a one-letter string that appears in word.
`Input: word = "a", forbidden = ["a"]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `ans = 1` instead of `0` → returns `1`

**Overlapping forbidden occurrences** - forbidden pattern repeats consecutively.
`Input: word = "aaaa", forbidden = ["aa"]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: only checking the longest L first and breaking after one match → may miss that moving left still leaves another "aa" inside, returns `2`

**Forbidden starts before left** - a forbidden substring would begin at an index < left.
`Input: word = "abc", forbidden = ["abc","bc","c"]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: not guarding `right-L+1 >= left` and updating left from an out-of-window start → can shrink left backward, returns `1`

**All characters forbidden** - every single letter is forbidden.
`Input: word = "ab", forbidden = ["a","b","ab"]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: forgetting to take `max(left, ...)` and instead assigning `left = right-L+2` unconditionally → returns `1`

followUps.q: What if forbidden strings could be up to length 1000?
followUps.a: Replace the inner O(L) substring+hash check with an Aho-Corasick automaton built over `forbidden`; feed `word` character by character and, at each position, use the failure links to find the longest forbidden suffix ending there, then move `left` past its start. Time becomes O(n + total forbidden length), space O(total forbidden length × alphabet).

followUps.q: What if `word` arrives as a streaming character stream of unknown length?
followUps.a: Keep the same window idea but only retain the last 10 characters in a ring buffer (since max forbidden length is 10); emit the running max when the stream ends. Memory drops to O(10) plus the forbidden set; time stays O(n).

followUps.q: What if you must also return one longest valid substring, not just its length?
followUps.a: Track the `(left, right)` pair whenever `ans` is updated, then return `word.substr(bestLeft, bestLen)` at the end. Time and space complexity are unchanged (the returned string is the output, not auxiliary).
